black.people: Existing six identities retained; Nell, Porter Wesley, White and Higginbotham add military recovery, bibliography, enslavement and theoretical/religious inquiry. Porter is explicitly a contributor. The selection remains weighted toward African American scholarship.
black.works_and_arguments: Brown’s and Woodson’s two baseline empty selections now contain works supported by primary prefaces and edition metadata. Existing representative prose survives. White and Higginbotham gain distinct works; Righteous Discontent remains metadata-only.
black.internal_distinctions: Four new approaches distinguish biographical recovery, collecting, enslaved women and racial analysis. Existing institution, Reconstruction and women approach IDs remain, with the last distinguishing professional and religious institutions.
black.incoming_connections: Higginbotham’s direct opening supports a productive but critical use of feminist theory. This later incoming contribution is explicitly separate from Black historiography’s independent origins. New Left and anti-colonial comparisons remain undirected.
black.outgoing_connections: Nell/military, Brown/biography and Black women/gender links now name projects and bounded evidence. Gilroy’s preface supplies direct Du Bois reception; Porter supplies a separate bibliographic contribution. James’s later Du Bois reception remains chronologically qualified.
black.evidence_and_interpretation: Primary prefaces, selected theoretical pages, retrospective institutional sources and metadata receive scoped checks. AAIHS date slips do not override existing dates, and a Rutgers default date is not treated as a real interview date. Later professional reception remains distinct from historical contribution.

atlantic.people: Bailyn receives a concrete pre-2000 work; Altman and Goveia broaden regional research. Mintz is reused with new shared Price; Porter Wesley and Du Bois gain contextual selections. All seven existing selections remain and generic source bundles are narrowed.
atlantic.works_and_arguments: The third baseline gap is filled with Bailyn’s 1986 Peopling introduction, separated from the 1988 paperback and 2005 Atlantic History. Altman’s primary introduction, Gilroy’s preface and scoped Goveia/Mintz-Price descriptions support distinct arguments.
atlantic.internal_distinctions: Five approaches add African contexts, migration/return, Caribbean slave society, cultural formation and diaspora archives. Oceanic scale, forced migration and diaspora critique do not become one method or uniform lineage.
atlantic.incoming_connections: Gilroy’s explicit use of Du Bois and named Hall resource clarify existing links. Mintz/Price supply an anthropological contribution with annotation-level evidence. James/Williams and Rodney retain their independent evidence and chronology.
atlantic.outgoing_connections: Altman supplies a specific migration/family contribution; the global comparison gains a local-scale example without an influence claim. Gilroy’s identity critique gains primary prefatory support while retaining its restricted object.
atlantic.evidence_and_interpretation: Primary introductions are distinguished from annotation, publisher description and catalogue evidence. Curtin’s numerical reconstruction and the 1999 database are not newly verified. Non-Anglophone and Indigenous historiographies remain underrepresented and explicitly queued.
